description: Source-lore pass 17 imports the five Abyss layers, their effects on cores and living creatures, the Infernal Core, and the Dragon Emperor's failed expedition.

entries.title: The Abyss
entries.summary: Below Kaysender's ordinary cloud layers lies a descending region of magical instability, toxic fog, violent winds, darkness, pressure, decay, despair, and failing reality.
body: The Abyss begins beneath the regular cloud layers as a treacherous, shifting expanse. Magical currents become unstable, natural energy thins, fog thickens, winds turn unpredictable, and darkness grows increasingly oppressive.

Descent is divided into the [[upper-abyss|Upper]], [[middle-abyss|Middle]], [[lower-abyss|Lower]], [[deep-abyss|Deep]], and [[deepest-abyss|Deepest Abyss]]. Each layer imposes greater strain on airship cores, operators, hulls, magic, breathing, perception, and sanity.

Airship cores lose efficiency, draw more heavily on operators, suffer feedback and lightning, and eventually approach total failure. Living creatures face low oxygen, toxic miasma, magical drain, physical decay, crushing pressure, illusions, psychic despair, and collapse of magic.
At the final depth lies the [[infernal-core|Infernal Core]], a molten realm from which the source says nothing returns.

sections.heading: Legacy Descent System
body: The source provides layer-specific Arcana, Constitution, piloting, repair, endurance, and survival checks with altitude loss, hull damage, exhaustion, magical failure, and death effects. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Upper Abyss
entries.summary: The first hundred feet below the normal clouds bring light magical turbulence, thin metallic fog, low oxygen, power fluctuations, and disorienting illusions.
body: The Upper Abyss is the shallowest layer, extending roughly one hundred feet beneath the ordinary cloud layers. Its air remains breathable, but thin metallic fog, magical disturbance, and oppressive atmosphere provide the first warning of deeper conditions.
Airship cores encounter localized surges and uneven energy flow. Ships may lose altitude or lurch when operators fail to fine-tune propulsion and compensate for turbulence.

Living creatures experience reduced oxygen, early fatigue, faint magical interference, and illusions that distort direction or perception. The layer is survivable, but it punishes crews who treat the descent as ordinary flight.

sections.heading: Legacy Layer Checks
body: The source uses moderate magical-control and turbulence checks, with gradual altitude loss and brief loss of control on failure. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Middle Abyss
entries.summary: At roughly two hundred feet, dense acrid fog, magical flux, heavy turbulence, energy feedback, and life-force erosion make continued descent dangerous.
body: The Middle Abyss extends to roughly two hundred feet beneath the clouds. Fog becomes dense and acrid, visibility contracts, and the atmosphere feels markedly heavier and more hostile.

Airship cores pull from unstable external energy while increased resistance demands more power to maintain lift. Sudden feedback surges through systems, and constant course correction becomes necessary.
Living creatures face erratic magical effects, breathing difficulty, reduced visibility, fatigue, and gradual erosion of magical and physical vitality.

sections.heading: Legacy Layer Checks
body: The source increases magical-control, endurance, and course-adjustment difficulty, with sudden drops, exhaustion, rolling, and hull stress on failure. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Lower Abyss
entries.summary: At roughly four hundred feet, elemental anomaly fields, sparse magic, toxic fog, crushing pressure, lightning, and aetheric distortion attack ships and creatures alike.
body: The Lower Abyss plunges to roughly four hundred feet and feels like a vast cavernous void. Its dense acrid fog is poisonous, atmospheric pressure increases, and magical interference becomes severe.

Elemental energies shift unpredictably around airship cores. Ambient magic is too sparse to sustain them easily, forcing greater demand on operators, while magical lightning damages propulsion and control systems.
Living creatures endure severe oxygen deprivation, magical decay, toxic air, and corrupted fields that distort spells and bodies. Repair work becomes both urgent and dangerous.

sections.heading: Legacy Layer Checks
body: The source uses high magical-management, endurance, and damage-control checks with rapid altitude loss, accumulating exhaustion, core damage, and reduced output. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Deep Abyss
entries.summary: At roughly eight hundred feet, corrupted magic, poisonous miasma, crushing pressure, lightning storms, magical void, and bodily rot make survival extraordinary.
body: The Deep Abyss reaches roughly eight hundred feet into an alien expanse. Poisonous miasmas drain life and magical essence, air becomes unfit for prolonged breathing, and crushing pressure exhausts bodies and structures.
Cores fight continuous magical disruption and draw directly from their operators. Persistent lightning targets ships while corrupted energy resists stabilization and shielding.
Living creatures face void-like depletion, extreme fatigue, and magical rot that gradually breaks down the body. Every minute spent here consumes reserves that cannot easily be restored.

sections.heading: Legacy Layer Checks
body: The source requires very high control, endurance, and shielding checks, with psychic injury, severe exhaustion, lightning damage, and rapid descent on failure. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Deepest Abyss
entries.summary: At roughly twelve hundred feet, magic, breathable air, navigation, physical endurance, and coherent thought collapse into total chaos and despair.
body: The Deepest Abyss reaches roughly twelve hundred feet and behaves as an otherworldly realm rather than ordinary sky. Time, space, and magic appear to break down amid dead magical residue and concentrated despair.
Airship cores surge, backfire, shut down, and resist repair. Magical currents toss ships without warning, while operators are pushed beyond physical and mental limits.

Living creatures face magical collapse, deathly miasma, suffocation, and mind-shattering despair. Continued descent leads toward the [[infernal-core|Infernal Core]], while failed recovery becomes an uncontrolled plunge.

sections.heading: Legacy Layer Checks
body: The source uses extreme maintenance, endurance, and repair checks with total core failure, incapacitation, catastrophic damage, and falling on failure. Conversion is required.

entries.title: The Infernal Core
entries.summary: The Abyss ends in a mile-wide molten realm of toxic ash, lava seas, collapsing volcanic islands, magical suppression, cursed heat, madness, and absolute finality.
body: The Infernal Core is a world within the bottom of the Abyss: roughly a mile across, enclosed by black walls of swirling darkness and filled with embers, volcanic plumes, fiery energy, and a central sea of magically corrupted lava.

Its air contains lethal ash, sulfur, and fumes. Heat mirages produce phantasmal distortions, while a black dome leaves only lava and eruptions for light. Temporary islands rise from the molten sea and collapse seconds or minutes later amid pyroclastic flows and debris.

The environment suppresses magic, drains airship cores, degrades enchantments, and makes navigation nearly impossible. Dwarven cores overheat; Elven cores enter feedback; Gnomish systems melt down; Dragon Kin cores may backfire despite their affinity for fire.

The Core carries a maddening aura and cursed lava. Short exposure can produce confusion, terror, obsession, violence, or sensory distortion; prolonged exposure may leave permanent madness requiring rare treatment.

There is no safe ground, breathable air, dependable spell, or stable escape. Ships disintegrate or explode before impact, and those reaching the lava sea are erased without recoverable wreckage. The source presents the Infernal Core as finality, not a destination to conquer.

sections.heading: Legacy Survival and Madness Rules
body: The source provides minute-scale breathing, heat, ash, lava, eruption, spell suppression, enchantment decay, core-specific failure, navigation, curse, and short- and long-term madness tables. Conversion is required.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: The Infernal Core: The Abyss's Final Layer

entries.title: The Lava-Born Horror
entries.summary: A colossal shifting titan of living lava dwells in the Infernal Core and destroyed the last companions of the future Dragon Emperor.
body: The Lava-Born Horror rose from the molten sea during the future Dragon Emperor's expedition. It appeared as a colossal living mass of fire and destruction, with black-pit eyes, lava-coated claws, and a body that churned like the sea around it.

It consumed two dragons with molten plumes, struck another from the sky, and swallowed Iragan the Stalwart after a final desperate battle. Its existence suggests that the Infernal Core is inhabited by forces able to kill even the mightiest dragonkind.

entries.title: The Dragon Emperor's Infernal Expedition
entries.summary: Before becoming Emperor, the proud young dragon led twelve companions into the Infernal Core; he alone returned, forever marked by their deaths and the cost of pride.
body: In his youth, the future Emperor of Dragons gathered twelve of the mightiest dragons of his age for an expedition motivated by bravado rather than necessity. The thirteen intended to prove that even the Abyss could not extinguish draconic power.

Confidence survived the Upper Abyss, but hostile magic, choking miasma, pressure, and despair broke formation and resolve layer by layer. Two dragons were lost in the Deepest Abyss before the survivors reached the molten Core.

There the [[lava-born-horror|Lava-Born Horror]] destroyed the remaining companions, including Iragan the Stalwart. Scorched and exhausted, the future Emperor abandoned conquest and escaped alone through every layer.

The experience dulled his scales and haunted his memory. In rare moments of drunken vulnerability, he tells the story as a warning: pride led twelve companions to deaths in a place never meant to be conquered.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: The Tale of the Emperor of Dragons and the Infernal Core
